Remember, I am not giving you legal advice and you should ask an attorney if you want a real answer, but my initial reaction is that there is no way walmart sues you for $150 unless they are out to make an example of you or something. A few more questions. So you never left the store with it? Did you do anything to the packaging? Was the letter delivered by personal delivery or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested? Which basically means, did you have to sign for the letter?

Weelllllllll the bad news is that if they took you to court you would lose. Damaging the property is enough under the statute for them to win. They could get the value of the property based on that.

They could get $300 and attorney fees and court costs under the statute. BUT the statute requires that they send the letter "by personal delivery or certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested." So that is the big thing for you right now and you need to figure out.

Based on the postage you said, they didn't. Certified mail costs a couple bucks, requires someone to sign, and there would be a thing on the outside of the envelope still saying it was sent via certified mail. It sounds like they didn't send it by the required methods. If they didn't, my guess is they send these out hoping that people will just give in out of fear but they want to keep the process as cheap as possible since so few people actually pay, so they send it by regular mail instead of the more expensive options that they actually need to under the statute.

Whatever you do, keep that envelope and letter so you have it if anything ever comes up.

And more importantly, stop stealing shit.

Just to show they didn't follow the appropriate process and then I have a loophole? So sorry for all the questions.

Sorry, I wasn't clear. They can sue you and win the value of the property no matter how they sent the letter assuming they follow proper court procedure for the actual case. But for them to get the $300 (or triple the value of the damaged good, whichever is greater) minimum damages, they can't use regular mail to send the letter. They also have to wait 30 days after the letter to file the complaint, so that could be another loophole in the future.

Don't lie and say you didn't get it. You will get yourself into more trouble. You want to keep everything that they sent so that if it does go to court, you can show the judge that it was sent via regular mail and not certified mail or any of the other options that are listed in the statute and I listed above. You really need to be sure of the method they sent it though for this all to apply. If it was sent with a stamp, it has to be through the USPS though, which means the statute requires it to be certified mail with a return receipt, which means someone would have had to sign and there would be something on the outside of the envelope still. The thing on the envelope is what links what you got to both what they sent and the slip of paper that would have been signed on delivery.

This is all based on this statute TITLE 51. TORTS - CHAPTER 10. INJURIES TO PERSONALTY - O.C.G.A. § 51-10-6 (2014)
